chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is no objection if a man permits his slave to purchase from his property, if he has a female slave or female slaves whom he may have intercourse with, and his slaves are permissible for him; and he said: It is permissible for the slave to marry two free women.

key_terms.جَارِيَة: Female slave, often used for concubinage
key_terms.رَقِيق: Plural of slave, referring to the class of slaves
key_terms.مَمْلُوك: Slave (male), specifically one owned by a master
key_terms.يَطَؤُهُنَّ: To have sexual intercourse with them (concubinage)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a slave to marry or buy slaves according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the juristic capacity of a male slave (mamluk) to engage in financial transactions and marriage, specifically permitting him to purchase female slaves for concubinage or to marry free women with his master's consent. It highlights the Shia legal view that a slave's acquired wealth and marital status are valid under specific conditions of ownership and permission, reflecting the nuanced status of 'abd' in classical fiqh.
